newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-June 4.

text.p: There are 27 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL said that social conditions are ripe for the Chinese government to re-evaluate the 1989 Tiananmen Square movement. It said that once China has gotten rid off its June 4 burden, it could concentrate on economic development. The paper asked since many dissidents have acknowledged that they went too far in 1989, why cannot the Chinese government admit its own mistakes in handling the event?

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said that mainland Chinese companies in the territory would not enjoy any priviledge after the handover and would not seek dominant positions. It said Hong Kong would remain capitalist and Chinese companies would also operate in the free market system. The paper said that mainland companies had been trying hard to mix into the local society, and it believed that they would gradually win the friendship and respect of local and foreign enterprises.

-- SING TAO DAILY said nobody doubted the determination of Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa to resolve the housing problem, but noted there was a huge gap between his promises and reality, which was proved by Tuesday's land auction. It said Tung should understand the relationship between Hong Kong's property market and general economy, otherwise, measures without thorough consideration could lead to harmful results.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said it had become clear that for all its protestations about non-intervention, the government was almost a dominant player in the property market. This intervention had been successful, said the paper, and the government should follow it up by increasing land supply.
